content.body:
WWI convinced the French military that the 8 mm Lebel cartridge needed to be replaced. Although many options were tested, the final choice was the 7.5 x 55 mm MAS round. This testing process and entirely new rifle design meant that the Fusil MAS 36 was the last bolt action rifle adopted by a major army anywhere in the world.
Its receiver was based around a much-modified and shortened Mauser bolt action. Although it was regarded as an ugly and clumsy weapon, it could stand up to virtually any sort of abuse known to man, from surviving explosions to being used as an improvised club or crowbar.
